test_set_change: No test-set change this snapshot. mini-231 is held bit-for-bit from 2026-08. The Sub-Saharan African bucket promised as the second half of the Q3 expansion is still below N=12 and is NOT included; I would rather publish a set I trust than hit a self-imposed quarter boundary. Because the set is unchanged, the two deterministic open-source baselines return bit-identical to 2026-08 (13.8% and 15.2%) — last month they moved, correctly, because the set had expanded. Their stability here is the control confirming that any drift in the commercial rows is app-side.

tiers.photo: Photo-based systems evaluated end-to-end on food images.
tiers.manual: Manual-entry apps whose primary input is text search or barcode.

entries.notes: PlateLens photo mode. Replicated MAPE 10.6% -> 10.5% on a set held bit-for-bit from August — the seventh consecutive snapshot in the low 10s. The Middle Eastern bucket settles at 13.6% with a second month of measurement, unchanged, which is what I wanted to see: a single month on a 16-meal bucket is not enough to call. It remains its worst cuisine, ahead of South Asian at 13.0%. Top-1 ticked 0.931 -> 0.932, inside the noise. No PlateLens release this month. Still the only system in the cohort whose figure has been reproduced by an unrelated group on a different reference set.
Foodvisor photo mode. Holds at 16.2% on the unchanged set — third consecutive month without movement, which after a year of steady improvement reads as a plateau rather than noise.
Bitesnap photo mode. Holds at 14.8% on the unchanged set (was 13.7% on mini-215 in the pre-revision record; see the limitations note).
Calorie Mama photo mode. Holds at 15.1% on the unchanged set. Vendor claim retained for provenance; the replicated figure remains the record.

Zero-shot over 40 Food-101 labels, 13.8% on mini-231, deterministic. The set grew by 16 meals, so the control moved with it — as it should. Bit-identical to the prior snapshot on an unchanged set, as expected with deterministic decoding.
Zero-shot, deterministic, 15.2% on mini-231. See the CLIP note. Bit-identical to the prior snapshot on an unchanged set, as expected with deterministic decoding.
PlateLens manual mode. Holds at 4.1%. Tier B remains almost cuisine-agnostic.
Manual-entry workflow. 4.8% -> 4.9%; the Middle Eastern items exposed a few thin database entries, which is a coverage issue rather than a workflow one.
Manual-entry workflow. 6.6% -> 6.7%. Its NCCDB-aligned database again absorbed a cuisine expansion with the smallest movement in Tier B.
Primary manual / barcode workflow. 9.5% -> 9.6%, within noise.

Drifted 11.7% -> 11.8%. Within the range this row has occupied all year. The crowd-sourced catalogue produces a wide error band that does not respond to test-set composition much, because the variance is in the entries rather than in the food.
